questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the US education system, and the UC system had one of the best academic reputations among my options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad program was at UC San Diego. Going there for the academics was a mistake - the upper division economics elective courses I took there were not very challenging. Had I known then, what I know now, I think I would have either avoided North America, or I would have taken the chance to do more courses outside of economics, as the breadth of your options far outweighs the depth.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy - campus was a mess to navigate, but I'd already figured out housing and courses prior to arrival. They were adamant in reminding us to fill out our necessary VISA documents.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I took part in th Solana Beach Host Family Program, which I highly recommend. I was picked up at the airport by my host family, stayed with them for a few days and got whatever help I needed from them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed at International House on campus, which was a great experience. Most people were around 20-21 years old, and it was a vibrant community. Friends of mine who stayed on campus, but outside of I-House mostly stayed people in their first or second year of college.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a mandatory meal plan, which worked basically like a gift card for the so-called dining halls on campus. The plan was enough for 1-2 meals per day. We had access to a kitchen with stovetop and oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was rather expensive. The whole thing ran me about 1700 dollars a month. I was expecting less from the information I'd previously found on the internet.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Received a 2-day timeslot where I was able to register for one or two courses. The option to sign up for the full allowed courseload was available later.
Had to upload a photo for my student ID and fill out a form, then had to show up at the place where I would be living, where I received the key to my appartement. Roommates had move-in times on different days, so we didn't all arrive at the same time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not sure - I found out what I needed for registration from information available online or in the registration portal.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got every class I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for courses early, and register for more than you intend to take. Dropping courses is easy in the first weeks of the semester/quarter, so you can keep the ones you like the best.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Course level seemed lower than at UCPH, and most of the other exchange students I met doing social science or management thought the courses were too easy. Friends doing science seemed to have a much harder time with the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
We had lectures similar to the ones at KU, and then TA office hours, where a PhD student would go through homework problems with us. I especially liked the professors office hours, where you could come by with problems with the material, and get great help.

Courses often had loads of assignments, which heavily influenced your final grade, meaning you had a fair bit of work, even though it wasn't very challenging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 121: Applied Econometrics and Data Analysis
ECON 129: Cities, Inequality, Innovation
ECON 130: Public Policy
ECON 131: Economics of the Environment
PHIL 12: Scientific Reasoning
DSC 10: Principles of Data Science
ECON 109: Game Theory
ECON 116: Economic Development
ECON 178: Machine Learning for Economics and Business
ECON 145: Economics of Ocean Resources (dropped)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend:
ECON 121 with Tom Vogl - reasonable course load, great office hours. I would have taken another course with him if I could.
ECON 129 with Fabian Eckert - fairly interesting, but not very challenging course. Eckert did an amazing job helping a friend of mine land a pre-doc position at Harvard.
PHIL 12 with Kerry McKenzie - very interesting course with engaging lectures.
DSC 10 - probably the best structured course I have ever taken. The homework problems amazing at helping you understand the material, it was a great way of learning the basics of Python.
ECON 116 with Sara Lowes - took this one out of interest, and boy, was it interesting.

I would avoid ECON 178 - lectures were a shit-show, and the course was poorly structured.
ECON 130 and ECON 131 were very easy with quite a bit of overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Amazing athetic facilities - picked up playing squash and racketball, and went to most of the uni basketball games. The gym was very close to international house. They also had lots of free concerts.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Basketball games were very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
1: Take a trip down to Mexico
2: Rent a car and drive up to Joshua Tree
3: Buy or rent a surf board and wetsuit

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly hung out with internationals - many of the local students have to move away from campus after year 2, so most of them don't stick around on campus after classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that I recall.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were generally outgoing

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try your best to get on-campus housing - the community at I-house is amazing.
Don't go there for the academics, you'll be let down.
Make the most of the non-academic campus opportunities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Professors are often more than willing to help you out - ask for a recommentation early, and they'll probably tell you what you need to do to get one. A few went above and beyond.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends we made along the way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting out of campus without a car was awful

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
